method: The real app was launched with SEANIME_SIDECAR=1 and SEANIME_DATADIR pointed at the isolated Phase 3/5 test profile, plus docs/migration/tools/fixture-manga-cdn.mjs on port 18846. Every call went renderer -> preload -> ipcMain -> main, i.e. the path the harness deliberately bypasses.
whatThisAddsOverTheHarness: The React component executed for the first time.
registerReadingIpc, the preload bridge and both new window.api methods were exercised.
The page bytes were rendered by a real in the real renderer.

readingMangaPageImage.note: THE DECISIVE LINE. The CDN 403s any request arriving without the provider header, so a 200 proves the Referer-style header survived renderer -> preload -> main -> CDN. Had the renderer loaded the URL directly in an , this would read 403.
readingMangaPageImage.imageNotVisuallyConfirmable: The fixture page is a 1x1 GIF, so the rendered occupies one pixel and cannot be seen in a screenshot. The CDN log and the pager state are the evidence; the harness separately proved the returned data URL decodes to byte-identical content.

pageCache.observed: Next page fetched page-2. Previous page issued NO new request.
pageCache.note: The 6-page bounded cache served the back-navigation, as designed.

incidentalFindings: Closing the Media workspace killed the sidecar with 'sidecar exited with code 1'. This is the documented no-client watchdog — `--desktop-sidecar` arms Seanime's dead-man switch and the workspace is what holds the websocket. Restarting from the dev panel recovered it. Reading Finder holds no websocket of its own, so a long provider-reading session will need the workspace open or the watchdog disarmed. Worth deciding before Phase 5 closes.
The first-run 'Put your country on the map?' consent dialog appeared and was declined, so nothing was sent.
cleanup: App closed (exit 0), sidecar gone, fixture CDN stopped, port 18846 released. 0 electron and 0 seanime processes remain. Anki was never involved.
